title: API vulnerabilities
goal_html: Students practice thinking like an API attacker: given a set of endpoint calls and an object-ownership table, decide which requests should be allowed and which are BOLA violations. Ties to LO 5.1.B (explain how the vulnerability is exploited).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and works through the mock API console, varying the object-ID parameter on each request and predicting allow/deny before submitting.
  2. For each BOLA violation found, partners write one sentence identifying which check the server skipped (authentication vs. authorization).
  3. Pairs then design one additional endpoint (e.g., GET /api/invoices/{id}) and write, in plain language, the server-side check that would prevent it from being BOLA-vulnerable.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "pentester" (chooses which object IDs to probe and predicts the result), the other is the "API developer" (proposes the missing ownership check and explains where in the request-handling code it belongs). Swap roles halfway through.
exit_html: Each student submits: one request they tested + whether it was a BOLA violation + the one-line server-side check that would fix it.
